comparison: Both address direct ORCA-KMT interactions (C27-C30). OpenEval finds evidence sufficient and SUPPORTED across multiple approaches. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing poor quality of endogenous co-IP data, concerns about overexpression artifacts, and requesting corroborating evidence beyond what is shown.

OpenEval R1 includes C31-C34 (catalytic activity requirement and domain mapping), which overlap with peer R2. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as part of converging evidence. Peer R2 addresses C31-C36 (chromatin context dependency) as UNCERTAIN, noting difficulty reconciling direct binding with chromatin-dependent interactions.

Both address chromatin context-dependency of ORCA-KMT interactions (C35-C36). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by CLTon experiments showing heterochromatin requirement. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, suggesting interactions may be chromatin-dependent rather than just chromatin-influenced, and that direct interactions may be too weak to detect in cells.

Both evaluate stoichiometry and complex formation claims (C37-C43, with peer also including C4). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by SiMPull analysis with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that all SiMPull assays use transient transfections, this is their first use of SiMPull for three-protein complexes, and explicitly requesting a second corroborating method (FRET, IP/re-IP).

Both address H3K9 methylation binding (C44-C46, with peer also including C2). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by peptide pull-downs and SiMPull analysis. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, with no specific concerns raised about these binding data.

Perfect claim overlap (C47-C52) on H3K9me3 levels after ORCA depletion. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, explaining the discrepancy between unchanged bulk Western blot and site-specific ChIP-seq decreases as due to resolution differences. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating they 'do not understand this apparent discrepancy' and finding the reduction at satellite repeats 'less than obvious,' undermining confidence in conclusions.

Perfect claim overlap (C53-C57) on ORCA enrichment and KMT chromatin association. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by ChIP-qPCR showing differential effects on Suv39H1 vs G9a. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised about these data.

Both address ORCA's scaffolding function (C58-C64, with peer also including C5, C9). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by loss-of-function and domain mutant experiments. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting key scaffolding points come from overexpressed proteins and explicitly requesting endogenous co-IP experiments with ORCA knockdown to demonstrate scaffolding, plus corroboration beyond SiMPull.

Both address replication timing effects (C67-C72, with peer also including C6-C8). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by multiple complementary approaches. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, fundamentally challenging the conclusion by stating experiments 'can't distinguish between heterochromatin-mediated origin firing effects and indirect effects of just having too little bound ORC' and noting all data come from cells with serious S phase defects.

Perfect claim overlap (C73-C81) on temporal depletion experiments separating ORCA's dual roles. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED, praising the experimental design. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, calling it a 'very key experiment' that 'didn't get the attention it deserves' and requiring critical controls: verification of ORC binding and complementation of si-ORCA depletion. They also question the biological importance of the smaller effects observed.

Both address major integrative conclusions and model (C10, C88, C100, C105, C107-C109, with OpenEval also including C2-C3, C9, C63). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though acknowledging speculative elements. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning the model and noting that if true, ORC knockdown alone should have little effect on heterochromatin—a control not performed. Concerns about distinguishing direct ORCA effects from ORC-dependent effects undermine the model.

Both address background/context claims about ORCA and ORC (C1, C11-C15). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established background. Peer R11 covers broader background including H3K9 methylation biology (C16-C26) and additional context claims (C82-C106), all rated SUPPORTED as established knowledge not challenged by reviewers.

OpenEval R12 addresses H3K9 methylation background (C16-C26) as SUPPORTED established literature. Peer R11 includes these claims within a larger set of background claims (C1, C11-C26, C82-C106), all rated SUPPORTED.

OpenEval R13 addresses extensive background/context claims (C65-C66, C82-C87, C89-C99, C101-C104, C106) as SUPPORTED by citations. Peer R11 includes substantial overlap of these background claims within its larger set, all rated SUPPORTED as established knowledge.

Minimal overlap (C65-C66) on heterochromatin organization background. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as part of broader context claims. Peer R12 specifically addresses C65-C66 as SUPPORTED by established literature (Towbin et al., 2012), providing context for localization changes.
